title: Ramayana: Part 1 Collects ₹64.10 Crore in Kerala in 17 Days
excerpt: Trade tracker AB George's figures show the Nitesh Tiwari epic rebounding in its third Kerala weekend, while Pinkvilla puts its all-India nett at ₹850.50 crore and its dubbed versions past a ₹200 crore first.
body:
• Ramayana: Part 1 has collected an estimated ₹64.10 crore gross in Kerala in its first 17 days, according to trade tracker AB George's figures reported by Filmibeat — putting the ₹70 crore mark within reach in its third week.
  • The film rebounded in its third weekend in the state: Day 17 brought about ₹3.75 crore, up from ₹2.35 crore on Day 16.
  • Across India, Pinkvilla puts the film's cumulative nett at ₹850.50 crore, with the South-dubbed versions crossing ₹200 crore nett — a first for the industry, the publication said.
  • Day 18 tracking on Sunday suggested another ₹4 crore-plus day in Kerala, but the final figure has not been confirmed.

Ramayana: Part 1 is closing in on ₹70 crore in Kerala. The Nitesh Tiwari epic has collected an estimated ₹64.10 crore gross in the state over its first 17 days, including 3D charges, according to figures shared by trade tracker AB George and reported by Filmibeat. Box office figures of this kind are trade estimates, not certified accounts — but the trend they show is consistent: after a mid-run dip, the film's Kerala collections rose again in its third weekend.

The Kerala run, week by week

The film took ₹28.50 crore in its extended eight-day opening week in Kerala, then added ₹29.50 crore in its second week — a rare second week larger than the first. Its best single day in the state so far was Day 11, at ₹6.75 crore. Collections eased to ₹2.40 crore on Day 15 and ₹2.35 crore on Day 16 before the third-weekend rebound: Day 17, on Saturday, brought approximately ₹3.75 crore. AB George's update on Sunday morning indicated Day 18 was heading toward crossing ₹4 crore, though the final Day 18 figure is yet to be confirmed.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=T0Uduwg2W2w

Kerala has been an unlikely stronghold for a Hindi epic. Earlier in the run, the film became the first Bollywood release to cross ₹20 crore in the state, passing the ₹19.50 crore reported for Dhurandhar 2. Pinkvilla, in its all-India report on November 21, said the film had grossed over ₹60 crore in Kerala and was en route to becoming the biggest non-Mollywood film in the state if the current momentum sustains.

The all-India picture

Nationally, Pinkvilla puts the film's cumulative nett at ₹850.50 crore after its third Friday, when it collected around ₹15 crore nett. Of the total, the Hindi version accounts for ₹649.75 crore nett and the dubbed versions for ₹200.75 crore nett. The South-dubbed versions crossing ₹200 crore nett is, Pinkvilla said, a first for the industry — a measure of how much of this film's audience is watching it in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam rather than in the original Hindi. Our earlier coverage tracked the five-language run that put Yash on the verge of a box-office first of his own.

About the film

Ramayana: Part 1 is the first instalment of a two-part adaptation of the Ramayana, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and written by Tiwari with Shridhar Raghavan, with Namit Malhotra and Yash backing the production. Ranbir Kapoor plays Rama, Yash plays Ravana, Sai Pallavi plays Sita, Ravi Dubey plays Lakshman and Sunny Deol plays Hanuman, with an ensemble that also includes Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan and Lara Dutta. The score is by Hans Zimmer and A. R. Rahman. The film was released worldwide in theatres on November 5, 2026, during the Diwali season, in Hindi with dubbed versions including Malayalam — and it remains in theatres now, in its third weekend, with the Kerala ₹70 crore milestone the next marker to watch.
